newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto posts loss, sees write-off for takeovers.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto posts loss, sees write-off for takeovers.

text.p: Monsanto Co. Friday reported a fourth-quarter loss after it took a one-time after-tax charge of $500 million to set up reserves for a restructuring that includes the spin-off of its chemical operations.

The company had a net loss of $410 million, or 69 cents a share, in the quarter, compared with profits of $80 million, or 13 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues edged up to $2.2 billion from $2.1 billion.
The results include the charge of 84 cents a share.

Monsanto plans to spin off its chemical operations later this year as it transforms itself into a life sciences company, focusing on agricultural, pharmaceutical and food ingredients businesses that it believes has greater growth potential.
Monsanto said it could write off as much as "a couple hundred million" dollars this year for research related to two acquisitions announced earlier this month.
Monsanto agreed to buy Holden's Foundation Seed Co. as well as distributors Corn States Hybrid Service and Corn States International for a total of about $1 billion.
Monsanto also agreed to buy Asgrow Agronomics from Mexico's Empresas La Moderna SA de CV for $240 million.
"There will be some in-process R&D write-off upfront," Monsanto Chief Economist Nicholas Filippello said. "For Holden's and Asgrow together, it could approach a couple hundred million upfront."
Filipello said Monsanto would shoulder unspecified amortization costs stemming from the acquisitions, particularly Holden's.
Filippello said Monsanto expected to maintain healthy margins in its life sciences operations.
Monsanto's stock fell $1 to $37.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
